headline: Cross-vendor agreement (synthetic, 3 providers): 91% across 15 constructed records
body: Automated reproducibility check: each constructed record was judged by 3 independent providers (anthropic, openai, google) (anthropic:claude-opus-4-8, openai:gpt-5, google:gemini-flash-latest); the figure is the share matching the most common answer. These are different vendors, so this is independent cross-vendor agreement. It is consistency on synthetic data only: not accuracy, not validation, and not evidence about real workplace records.
observation: On the same 15 constructed records, 3 independent providers (anthropic, openai, google) gave the same answer about 91% of the time. These are different vendors, so this is independent cross-vendor agreement. Agreement is not accuracy and not validation.
research_question: When 3 independent providers (anthropic, openai, google) judge the same record, does 91% agreement reflect a stable signal in the record, shared behavior, or prompt design? Reproducibility is distinct from accuracy and from validation.
discussion: 3 independent providers (anthropic, openai, google) agreed about 91% of the time on synthetic records. Why might independent models still agree without being right, and what evidence would change your confidence?
debate: Does independent cross-vendor agreement on synthetic records tell us anything about real-record accuracy?

poll.question: Which would raise your confidence in a review result the most?

challenge: Take the One-Minute Challenge on the same kind of record and compare your read to the model’s.
supporting_data: 15 constructed (synthetic) records · 3 independent providers (anthropic, openai, google) (anthropic:claude-opus-4-8, openai:gpt-5, google:gemini-flash-latest), one pass each · no human reviewers, no ground-truth labels

headline: Human inter-rater reliability: substantial agreement (Gwet's AC1 0.74 experts, 0.63 trained reviewers)
body: Independent raters applied the five JRS conditions to a shared set of 10 constructed records. Expert raters (about 3.6 per record) reached Gwet's AC1 = 0.74; trained reviewers (about 7.2 per record) reached AC1 = 0.63. Both fall in the substantial range, and the reviewer coefficient clears the pre-registered floor of 0.61. Reliability means reviewers apply the standard consistently; it is not accuracy and not validation.
observation: On 10 constructed records, independent expert and trained reviewers applying the five JRS conditions agreed at a substantial, chance-corrected level (Gwet's AC1 0.74 and 0.63 respectively).
research_question: Do independent reviewers apply the five JRS conditions consistently, above chance?
supporting_data: 10 records; 8 experts and 16 trained reviewers; 108 labeled determinations. Gwet's AC1 primary per the pre-registered analysis plan (methodology: Ubayet Hossain, FRM, Associate Director, Model Validation, KPMG India).
